title: CounterCount: Diagnosing Knowledge Bias in How Vision-Language Models Count Attributes
abstract: arXiv:2605.17826v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Do Vision-Language Models (VLMs) count what they see, or what they know about the world? We introduce CounterCount, a diagnostic dataset of paired factual and counterfactual (CF) images, in which the CF image contains an atypical count of a subject's attribute (e.g., a rabbit with four ears), together with annotations localizing the counted attributes. Humans answer both types of images nearly perfectly ($98.9\%$ and $97.5\%$), but across 16 VLMs (14 open-weight and 2 closed-source), average accuracy drops from $91.6\%$ on factual to $49.5\%$ on CF images, with most errors stemming from responses that match the canonical count, therefore revealing a bias towards knowledge priors rather than reliance on visual information. Based on these findings, we perform an analysis that reveals two interesting insights behind this gap. First, models exhibit a ``System-1''-like response behavior, falling back on canonical counts after a shal

translated_title: CounterCount：诊断视觉-语言模型在属性计数中的知识偏差
translated_abstract: 视觉-语言模型（VLM）数的是它们所看到的，还是它们所知道的世界？我们提出了CounterCount，这是一个由成对的事实性和反事实（CF）图像组成的诊断数据集，其中反事实图像包含某主体属性的非典型数量（例如，一只长有四只耳朵的兔子），并附带定位被计数属性的标注。人类对两类图像的回答几乎完美（98.9%和97.5%），但在16个VLM（14个开源权重模型和2个闭源模型）上，平均准确率从事实性图像上的91.6%骤降至反事实图像上的49.5%，且大多数错误源于回答与典型数量相一致的结果，从而揭示了模型偏向知识先验而非依赖视觉信息。基于这些发现，我们进行的分析揭示了这一差距背后的两个有趣见解。首先，模型表现出类似“系统1”的响应行为，在浅层处理后便回退到典型计数……
tldr: 提出了CounterCount诊断数据集，通过成对的事实性与反事实图像揭示视觉-语言模型在计数时依赖知识先验而非视觉信息的偏差——反事实图像上准确率从91.6%骤降至49.5%。
en_tdlr: CounterCount, a diagnostic dataset of paired factual and counterfactual images, reveals that vision-language models rely on knowledge priors rather than visual evidence when counting attributes, with accuracy dropping from 91.6% to 49.5% on counterfactual images.
